tldr: At the headline layer, 44 outlets across 22 country groups converge overwhelmingly on a CAPACITY_RESOURCES frame: the US seizing majority control of 65 billion barrels of Venezuelan oil dominates homepage-level language in triumphalist terms ('biggest oil deal in world history,' 'MORE THAN DOUBLES U.S. Oil Reserves'). A secondary EXTERNAL_REGULATION frame — Venezuela asserting 'sovereignty' despite the deal — appears distinctively in Al Jazeera, El País, G1, and South China Morning Post headlines, making the same agreement look like a sovereignty concession rather than a triumph. A POLITICAL frame (Democratic alarm, Venezuelan factional splits) surfaces mainly in US and French international outlets. German-language media (Sueddeutsche, ZDF) are the only outlets to inject editorial skepticism directly into the headline, framing expert doubt while Anglophone titles relay Trump's superlatives uncritically.
event_summary: The US and Venezuela announced a sweeping 25-year oil deal giving American interests majority control of 65 billion barrels of Venezuelan oil reserves; Trump called it the 'biggest oil deal in world history' while Venezuela's interim president Delcy Rodríguez defended it as preserving sovereignty and targeting 1.5 million barrels per day of production.

paradox: Both sides simultaneously claim victory at headline level: US outlets trumpet 'biggest oil deal in world history' and 'MORE THAN DOUBLES U.S. Oil Reserves,' while Venezuelan and Latin American outlets lead with 'retains sovereignty' — the same agreement is framed as US dominance by one bloc and Venezuelan sovereignty preservation by the other, a contradiction visible purely at the title layer.

single_outlet_findings.finding: The only outlet to combine 'boasts' and 'takeover' in a single headline — 'Trump boasts US takeover of Venezuela's vast oil reserves' — deploying the most adversarial framing of US intent in the entire corpus, harder than RT's 'claims' and sharply contrasting with the neutral 'announces' used by most Anglophone peers.

The sole outlet to use all-caps shouting ('MORE THAN DOUBLES') as a headline intensifier — a tabloid-register device absent from all 43 other outlets — magnifying the triumphal frame to its loudest pitch.

The only outlet to embed expert skepticism directly in the headline with an interrogative — 'Der "größte Öl-Deal der Weltgeschichte"? Experte skeptisch' — foregrounding analytical doubt while every Anglophone outlet relays Trump's superlatives without punctuation-level challenge.

The sole outlet to invoke the morality register at headline level — 'Trump Taking Venezuelan Oil Is "Morally Wrong"' — quoting Democratic Congressman Ro Khanna in a frame designed to expose opposition critique rather than report the deal itself; no other outlet deploys moral language in its title.

bottom_line: The headline layer reduces this sweeping geopolitical energy agreement to a single dominant image — the US seizing 65 billion barrels of oil — with sovereignty pushback and political fracture as secondary signals, while deeper economic analysis, legal structure, and diplomatic implications remain entirely below the fold across all 44 outlets.
